18:04 · ONE MESSAGE · SIX QUESTIONS IT DOES NOT ANSWER02 / 17

The order is not the hard part. The missing facts are.

Which Gula — the 1 kg pack or the 2 kg pack?
Which tier price does this customer buy on?
Is the onion in stock, and how much of it?
Does “kalau ada” reduce the line, or drop it?
Does RM2.80 sit below her tier price?
Which egg grade — A, B or C?
Six facts. The message is synthetic; the six questions are ours. One clerk settles all six today — from memory, at the end of the day.

THREE ANSWERS ALREADY EXIST04 / 17

All three optimise the message. None can supply a fact the message does not contain.

01

By hand

Ask the customer, read the price file, walk to the whiteboard, type the delivery order.

Nothing is wrong except the time — and it collapses when eleven messages land at once.
02

A translating bot

Malay, Chinese and English become a clean, structured order list.

The list looks perfect and is still wrong. Pack size is not a language problem.
03

A flag-everything checker

Suspicious lines turn red and the flow stops for a human.

A red flag is a question, not an answer. The work still ends with the clerk.

WHAT WE DO DIFFERENTLY05 / 17

The model proposes. Rules settle. A named person decides.

01 · THE MODEL

It proposes. It never prices.

Product candidates, quantities, units, pack sizes and source spans — restricted to the tenant catalogue, or an explicit UNKNOWN.

It cannot set a price, approve an order, or issue a delivery order.
02 · THE RULES

Facts come from her own data.

Tier price, stock and pack size are computed from the merchant's own catalogue and price file, never generated.

A field the data cannot evidence becomes a blocking issue, never a plausible guess.
03 · THE PEOPLE

A named person signs.

A clerk clears routine orders. The owner decides a below-tier price, and can reject with a reason.

The warehouse sees picking detail with no prices and no contact numbers.

HOW WE EARN MONEY07 / 17

Charged per approved order. Never per seat.

  • Billing unit: one approved delivery order. Parsing, fallback, rejection and discard are free — we charge only when the merchant got a delivery order she approved.
  • A free tier runs on the rules path: no model call, so a merchant can adopt the discipline of approval and audit before paying anything.
  • Measured cost anchor: US$0.00019 per GPU-second on one 24 GB card; at p50 1.93 s per parse that is about US$0.4 per 1,000 orders — model time only, idle GPU excluded.
  • The price is not set. Freemium — N free orders a month, then per order — is validated by interview in the pilot. We will not print a number we cannot defend.
Per-order revenue follows work the merchant actually accepts, not seats she hopes to fill.

HE MINGHAO · BACKEND & RULES09 / 17

Where the numbers come from.

INNOVATION

The model never prices.

Every price, every stock quantity and every pack size is computed from the merchant's own catalogue — never generated. A field the data cannot evidence becomes a blocking issue instead of a plausible guess.

CORE TECHNOLOGY

An approval state machine with a permission matrix.

Unsaved edits cannot be approved. A below-tier price cannot pass without the owner. A cross-tenant read returns 404 — enforced at the API, not hidden on the page.

Falcons · KiraOrder for Orbyte4:08–5:08
XIONG PEICHENG · AI & DEPLOYMENT10 / 17

When the model cannot answer, failure is visible.

INNOVATION

Failure is visible.

Deterministic fallback, the extraction mode on screen, and no silent guess. If the model is unavailable, the UI shows FALLBACK. If a field is not evidenced, it becomes a blocking issue — not a guess.

CORE TECHNOLOGY

An evidence-bound AI contract.

Qwen proposes product, quantity, unit and pack. The backend verifies each proposed field against the source span; unsupported fields are blocked, not guessed. Price, stock and approval are never decided by the model.

YE LIANGHUI · FRONTEND11 / 17

Make uncertainty actionable.

INNOVATION

The screen shows both options.

Ten trays of eggs, no grade. Instead of choosing for the clerk, the card puts the two catalogue options side by side — each with its own price and its own stock.

CORE TECHNOLOGY

A dispute becomes a card and a question.

The unresolved line names the field, keeps the span it came from, and drafts the question for the customer. The next step is “Resolve checks”. Approval must wait.

ZHOU JINGXI · DATA & QUALITY13 / 17

We score against an answer key the model did not write.

INNOVATION

Strict whole-case scoring.

A case passes only when all six fields are right at once. Eight of twenty-three do. Small sample, built by us — and we report the number as it is.

CORE TECHNOLOGY

A frozen set with hashes, and two tenants on one build.

Every frozen file carries a SHA-256, so a re-run can be checked rather than trusted. The same build serves a food catalogue and a hardware catalogue.

DEMO BACKUP · WHEN IT CANNOT BE SURE15 / 17

It stops — and it stops at the right desk.

01Edit a line but do not save → Approve stays disabled. Unsaved edits cannot be approved.
02Record a below-tier price on the Gula line → Send to owner → the draft locks while it waits.
03Owner role: an empty rejection reason is refused → reject with a reason → order closed.
04Reopen the draft: closed. No approve, no save, no delivery order.
The point is the disabled button and the closed order, not the enabled one.If the owner queue is empty, open the seeded pending request. This assumes Local Demo.
